Subject: Re: Brief downtime window — requesting RCA and timeline

Hi Marissa,

We saw a ~45s window of elevated token latency and a small percentage of 500s between 14:47 and 14:53 PST today. This affected a handful of checkout flows; our SRE flagged it and we briefly routed traffic to a fallback model. Appreciate a clear timeline and what you plan to do to make sure this doesn’t recur.

Can you also confirm whether any customer data left our region or whether logs we provided earlier were sufficient?

Thanks,
Sara
Director, Platform Reliability
HarborPay

Hi Sara — thanks for the heads up and the data you already sent. We're investigating now. Initial notes:
- We observed degraded tail latency correlated with a model shard failover and an unexpectedly large sequence-length spike for some sessions.
- No evidence so far of cross-region data transfer — logs point to in-region retry loops.

Can you share the request IDs you saw around 14:48? That will let us correlate KV-cache hits/misses.

I'll coordinate a short technical readout tomorrow morning and aim to provide an annotated timeline + remediation checklist within 24 hours.

Best,
Marissa
Principal Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference

Internal note for timeline:

- 14:45 PST: we detected elevated per-token latency and started draining affected worker.
- 14:47–14:53 PST: tail latency spike and ~0.6% 500s due to in-flight KV cache misses + shard reattachment latency.
- 14:55 PST: service autoscale and sticky routing stabilized, error rate returned to baseline.

From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Li <sara.li@harborpay.com>, support@harborpay.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 18:02:00 -08:00
Subject: Service Stability Briefing and Remediation Promise

Sara — thank you for your patience and for the detailed traces your team shared. Below is our customer-facing summary of findings, an annotated timeline, and concrete remediation actions we will deliver and the deadlines we commit to.

Executive summary
- What happened: on 2026-11-29 at ~14:47 PST a subset of inference workers experienced a coordinated set of events: an autoscaler scale-down raced with long-sequence requests, leading to KV-cache eviction + shard reattachment latency. That combination produced a tail-latency spike and a small increase in 5xx responses.
- Impact: HarborPay saw elevated latency for a small fraction of requests (~0.6% 500s) concentrated in a 6-minute window; no customer data left the configured region.
- Root cause: autoscaler configured with an aggressive scale-down window combined with unanticipated long-sequence session traffic. The scale-down evicted shards while some sessions were still holding large KV caches, triggering reattachment events that increased processing latency.

Annotated timeline (UTC and PST)
- 2026-11-29 22:40 UTC (14:40 PST): autoscaler initiated scale-down of pool-a (policy: 60s idle).
- 2026-11-29 22:45 UTC (14:45 PST): several customer sessions sent sequences > max-seq seen historically; KV cache pressure increased.
- 2026-11-29 22:47 UTC (14:47 PST): worker drain + shard eviction coincided with reattachment, causing increased request processing time and a ~6-minute error window.
- 2026-11-29 22:55 UTC (14:55 PST): routing and cache warm-up restored baseline latency.

Actions we are taking (ownership and committed dates)
1) Immediate rollout (within 48 hours): increase autoscaler conservative window to prevent scale-down during sustained long-sequence traffic; add pre-drain check for active KV cache size. Owner: Platform Reliability Ops (Kimberly).
2) Short-term mitigation (2 weeks): implement a fast reattachment path for KV shards that prioritizes in-flight sessions to reduce reattachment latency. Owner: Runtime Engineering (Marissa & Kevin Patel).
3) Medium-term control (8 weeks): adaptive autoscaling policy that considers sequence-length distribution and KV cache pressure, plus a canary rollout for safety. Owner: Serving Runtime Team; we will share design doc by 2026-12-14.
4) Audit & verification (4 weeks): we'll run a full verification exercise with HarborPay test tokens in a staging environment that mirrors your peak mix. We'll invite your SREs to a verification run; proposed window: week of 2026-12-07. Owner: Customer Success + Reliability.
5) Compensation discussion: we will credit HarborPay for measurable impact consistent with our SLA. I’ve looped in our account team to start that conversation.

Attached to this email: partial-rca.pdf (annotated findings), annotated-timeline.csv (request id correlation), remediation-checklist.xlsx (owners & deadlines).

Data security and scope
- No logs or data were exfiltrated; all activity was in-region. We encrypted all logging artifacts at rest and in transit.

Next steps for HarborPay
- Please confirm two available windows for the verification-run during week of 2026-12-07.
- If you have additional request IDs or traces, attach them to the Drive link above and we’ll fold them into the timeline.

We regret the disruption and take this seriously. These actions are designed to both eliminate the immediate failure mode and reduce the likelihood of reoccurrence under atypical sequence-length distributions. I’ll be your point contact for the remediation roadmap — reach me directly if anything urgent comes up.

Best regards,

Markus Klein
VP, Customer Engineering
Redwood Inference
